## Question

**Do people cluster with the friends they expect to?** I designed a 121-question survey covering personality, politics, social "tribes" and pop culture, then built an interactive map so respondents could compare who they're actually most similar to with who they guessed.

## Data

- Real survey: 53 respondents from my friend group. This data is kept private.
- Public demo: a [synthetic dataset](https://github.com/emckay2028/friendship-explorer) with 34 fake respondents and the same 121-column schema.

## Method

- Turned survey responses into separate feature matrices for each dimension.
- Computed pairwise similarity and showed it as **within-person percentile ranks**, because raw similarity scores produced many ties.
- Laid out respondents with **PCA and a repulsion layout**, coloured by cluster.
- When a user hides dots, the layout **recomputes for the visible subset**, so clusters tighten around the people still shown.

## Features

- Seven views: Overall, Personality, Politics, Tribes and three pairwise combinations, each with its own rankings and cluster signatures.
- Hover cards showing each person's top five matches, plus name search and pinning.
